chunks: The illustrious Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babuwayh al-Qummi (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who said:
Sleep is the relaxation of the body, speech is the relaxation of the soul, and silence is the relaxation of the intellect.

key_terms.السكوت: Silence — the restraint that gives rest to the intellect
key_terms.النطق: Speech — the expression that gives rest to the soul
key_terms.النوم: Sleep — rest of the physical body

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq say about sleep, speech, and silence?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) succinctly describes the three forms of rest: sleep for the body, speech for the soul, and silence for the intellect. This tripartite teaching, delivered in the assembly of 368 AH, reflects Islamic wisdom about the holistic balance of human faculties and the need to attend to each dimension of the self.

en.bilal-muhammad: Abu Ja`far Muhammad b. `Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babuwayh al-Qummi (rh) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan b. Ahmad b. al-Walid (ra) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us. He said: Al-`Abbas b. Ma`ruf narrated to us from Sa`dan b. Muslim from Abi `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as). He said:
Sleep is the relaxation of the body, speech is the relaxation of the soul, and silence is the relaxation of the intellect.
